candidates.title: If Agents Were Angels, No Governance Would Be Necessary: Out-of-Band Policy Enforcement at a Trusted Tool Boundary
candidates.citationVelocity: Published ~11 days ago (submitted 2026-08-27); Semantic Scholar: 0 citations
communitySignals: No Papers with Code repo found
Authors' company has a corresponding production offering (Redpanda Agentic Data Plane) referenced in the paper
credibilityEvidence: Section 8 Table 4: descriptive rates across 4 models (raw/prompt/prompt+OBPE) for 6 failure metrics and 5 success metrics
Section 8: cluster-weighted paired analysis, 3,621 trials, trace failure 57.6%->0.2%, 41.2pp reduction [95% CI 27.7,54.9], every model-specific estimate favored OBPE
Section 8 RQ2b: cumulative operator ablation ladder (record controls -> field stripping -> masking+write guard -> pattern masking), each rung's marginal contribution reported with CI
Section 8: sensitivity analysis assigning 46 unknown-outcome trials in both worst-case directions (range 33.8-43.1pp, still favors OBPE); leave-one-cluster-out range 39.4-42.4pp
Section 8: honest failure disclosure - 4 exact-value reconstructions and 1 row-count oracle leak explicitly reported as unresolved
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Covers main effect (RQ1), robustness without prompt rules (RQ2a), component ablation (RQ2b), comparison to output-review baseline (RQ3), a red-team stress slice, and formal proofs of order-independence and monotone narrowing
reproducibilityEvidence: Paper states a simplified HTTP proxy prototype based on the production OBPE implementation is released, with Cedar policy schema and conformance tests
No independently confirmed public GitHub URL located in the fetched sections
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Large controlled trial with formal guarantees plus honest disclosure of residual leak paths supports the article's claim strength
candidates.primaryLimitation: Evaluated on controlled Jira/ServiceNow mocks (not live production); 116 trials affected by a query-evaluator defect in the mock; 4 final answers still reconstructed exact values that never entered context
candidates.presentationReason: Explicit threat model, staged composition formalized with proofs, results separated into RQ1-RQ3 with clearly stated evidence boundaries
candidates.reason: Strongest of today's candidates on evidence rigor: large controlled trial (3,621 trials, 4 models, adaptive red-team) with formal order-independence proof and an honest ablation ladder isolating each protection layer's contribution; reentered from watch after two prior rounds (2026-09-01, 2026-09-06) where it was deferred for thematic diversity, not credibility concerns.

candidates.title: Polished but Unresolved: Identifying Late-Stage Pressure States in Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents
candidates.venue: EMNLP 2026 (self-reported accepted, per arXiv Comments field: "Accepted in the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing")
candidates.citationVelocity: Published 6 days ago (submitted 2026-09-01); Semantic Scholar: 0 citations
candidates.institution: Not stated in paper; author emails are personal (gmail/taobao) addresses
communitySignals: No Papers with Code repo found
credibilityEvidence: Section 3: behavioral evidence (density map of CS vs DPS) plus linear-probe ROC/PR results showing pressure state is linearly separable in hidden space
Section 4: activation-intervention results showing causal link between pressure direction and continue-vs-submit behavior
Section 5 Table 3: constraint-clarity and action-mapping mitigation results with attention-concentration analysis (19.1% of attention mass on 11.9% of prefill tokens)

Section 7 Tables 4-6: 3 backbones (Qwen3-14B/32B, OLMo-3.1-32B) x 3 scaffolds (CoT/ReAct/Reflexion) on DeepPlanning-Travel, generalization to DeepPlanning-Shop and TravelPlanner, and ablation with random/periodic-trigger controls ruling out the 'any intervention helps' confound
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Full causal chain from detection through intervention, mitigation factors, and the PSPR controller is quantitatively tested; two-fold held-out evaluation for the probe avoids overfitting; trigger-timing ablation controls for a key confound
reproducibilityEvidence: Method, thresholds (a=0.4, b=0.65), and prompts described in the paper/appendix
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Complete causal chain plus confound-ruling-out controls support the claim that late-stage pressure is a real, actionable internal state
candidates.primaryLimitation: Validation concentrates on travel/shopping planning tasks with clearly verifiable hard constraints; the white-box probe method requires hidden-state access and does not transfer to API-only commercial models as-is; TravelPlanner's strict Final score did not improve
candidates.presentationReason: Method section separates detection, mitigation-factor analysis, and the PSPR controller cleanly; ablation and control conditions are explicitly delineated from the main result
candidates.reason: Fresh Layer A find via SKILL.md Q1 query; selected for providing the first mechanistic, intervenable account of a widely-observed but previously only behaviorally-described failure mode (premature closure in long-horizon agents), with a confound-controlled ablation that most agent papers skip.

candidates.title: Control-Data Flow Separation: Stable Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent LLMs
candidates.venue: EMNLP 2026 Findings (registered in arXiv's Journal reference field)
candidates.citationVelocity: Published 6 days ago (submitted 2026-09-01); Semantic Scholar API rate-limited on repeated attempts this run, citation count not-assessed
communitySignals: No Papers with Code entry found
credibilityEvidence: Section 4: 4 evaluation settings (BBH single-agent reasoning, MARG multi-agent review generation, synthetic + industry-verified insurance underwriting) with 100% eventual protocol validity vs naive TextGrad's collapse
Section 5.1 Table 2: 3-axis ablation (schema scaffolding / parse retry / per-example feedback) isolating each component's contribution to stability vs quality gains
Section 5.2 Table 3: prompt-edit control-surface-touch analysis (16.6% vs 4.2% of edited lines) explaining the mechanism of naive TextGrad's collapse
Section 5.3 Table 4: 3-model-family robustness test (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google) showing 100% stability for the proposed method across all three vs 0% for naive
Limitations section explicitly states protocol validity does not guarantee output correctness
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Main effect, mechanism-isolating ablation, cross-model-family robustness, and a real industry (insurance underwriting) deployment scenario are all covered with quantitative results
reproducibilityEvidence: Claimed <40 lines of Python for a complete pipeline
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Clean ablations isolating stability vs quality mechanisms, cross-model-family robustness, public code, and an explicit stated limitation on correctness vs stability
candidates.primaryLimitation: Guarantees protocol validity, not semantic correctness; authors explicitly state a protocol-valid pipeline can still produce incorrect or low-quality outputs
candidates.presentationReason: Formalizes the control/data distinction with a stated protocol-stability lemma, and separates 'what the model proves' from 'what the benchmark observes' throughout
candidates.reason: Fresh Layer A find via SKILL.md Q3 query, peer-reviewed (EMNLP 2026 Findings) with released code and an industry-verified evaluation setting; selected for exposing an underdiscussed failure mode (prompt optimizers corrupting execution protocol) as the third leg of today's trust-boundary theme.
